one_liner: The safe all rounder. Handles daily runs, treadmill sessions and the odd parkrun without fuss.
Thick, soft and forgiving underfoot. Great value if you want maximum comfort on easy runs.
Nike's softest everyday shoe. Bouncy foam that makes long, slow miles feel much easier.
Steady and supportive if your ankles roll inwards. Built to last a lot of miles.
A carbon plated trainer for faster sessions. Race day feel that survives everyday training.
Feather light race shoe for 5k up to marathon. Save it for the big days.
Nike's flagship marathon shoe. Springy air pods and a carbon plate for one big effort.
A road shoe feel with proper grip. Good for towpaths, parks and light trails.
Tough and grippy for muddy, rocky British trails. Underfoot protection without feeling clumsy.
Soft, protective and forgiving. The default choice for comfortable everyday miles.
Softer and cheaper than the Nimbus. A sensible first proper running shoe.
Bouncy and fun but still cushioned. Happy plodding along or picking up the pace.
The classic support shoe. Plush, stable and very hard to fall out with.
Gentle support at a fair price. A reliable starting point if you need stability.
Tall, light and lively. Expensive, but it can do almost every type of run.
Light carbon plated shoe for faster running. A cheaper way into race style shoes.
Very light racing shoe built for runners who lengthen their stride at speed.
A dependable everyday trail shoe. Good grip, decent cushioning and it lasts well.
Soft, roomy and easy going. Adidas' straightforward shoe for regular training runs.
Cushioned support with a generous fit. Quietly keeps your foot tracking straight.
Adidas' softest everyday cushion. Made for slow, comfortable miles rather than speed.
Light, springy and great value. A favourite for faster runs and shorter races.
Firm and purposeful with rods for push off. Best when you want to work.
Adidas' top marathon racer. Very light, very fast and fits on the narrow side.
Comfy and hard wearing but heavy. Better for walking and gentle jogs than training.
Light and quick on the trails. Aimed at long off road races rather than beginners.
Waterproof and grippy for wet British winters. Keeps your feet dry on soggy paths.
Soft, light and easy to run in. Hoka's most popular everyday shoe for good reason.
About as much cushioning as you can buy. Great if your legs and joints ache.
Light and springy without being a race shoe. Good for picking up the pace.
Gentle support built in without feeling stiff. A light, friendly stability shoe.
Maximum support and cushioning together. Built for feet that roll inwards a lot.
Hoka's fastest carbon race shoe. Aggressive, expensive and only for race day.
The default trail shoe for muddy UK paths. Loads of grip and cushioning.
Half road shoe, half trail shoe. Ideal if your runs mix pavement and parks.
The safe, do everything trainer. If you are unsure what to buy, start here.
A big, wide, forgiving platform. Very stable underfoot and kind to sore joints.
Brooks at its softest. A pricey but very comfortable shoe for steady miles.
The classic support shoe. Sold in more widths than almost anything else out there.
The cheapest sensible Brooks. Firmer and lighter, and fine for a first pair.
Tall, bouncy and rolls you forward. A cheaper stand in for a race shoe.
Brooks' carbon plated racer. Very light, very fast, and saved for race day.
A tough, steady trail shoe with Vibram grip. Handles rough ground and wet rock.
A well balanced everyday shoe. Light enough to speed up, soft enough to plod.
Deep, soft cushioning that stays surprisingly light. One of the best long run shoes.
Quiet support that most people never notice. A good first stability shoe.
Loads of soft foam with support built in. Light for how much shoe it is.
A plated shoe you can actually train in every week. Fast but not fragile.
A proper carbon marathon racer that stays stable. Save it for your goal race.
Grippy, low to the ground and sure footed. Great on technical or muddy trails.
Cushioned trail shoe for very long days out. Heavy but protective and grippy.
Soft, roomy and light for its size. Comes in 2E and 4E widths.
A sturdy, no drama trainer that lasts. Widths up to 4E if you need room.
Solid, supportive and heavy. Best if you want obvious control and a roomy fit.
Light, bouncy and fun without a plate. A favourite for faster training runs.
A huge slab of soft foam. Made for slow, comfortable miles and recovery days.
New Balance's top marathon racer. Very light, very soft and built to go fast.
A plated, super cushioned trainer for marathon build ups. Soft with a forward roll.
Cushioned trail shoe with Vibram grip and rare wide fittings. Comfortable on rough ground.
Soft and easy going everyday shoe that suits steady runs and shorter distances.
Big, bouncy and fun underfoot, good for easy miles when your legs feel heavy.
Steady, supportive and forgiving, a safe first proper running shoe for most people.
Very light carbon plated racer built for going fast on race day.
Brilliant value all rounder that does easy runs and faster days without fuss.
One shoe that handles long runs, faster sessions and a half marathon happily.
Loads of soft foam underfoot, so long slow miles feel a lot kinder.
Firm rim around soft foam keeps wobbly ankles in line on longer runs.
Feather light race shoe for runners chasing a personal best over 10k or more.
Dependable everyday trainer that lasts well and rarely gives anyone trouble.
Classic support shoe for feet that roll inwards, tough and built to last.
Thick, soft and protective, a comfy pick for recovery runs and long days.
Tall stack with a plate, so long runs roll along quicker than expected.
Roomy toes and a completely flat platform, ease into it over a few weeks.
Wide toe room with a small heel lift, the friendliest way into Altra.
Cult trail shoe with masses of toe room and grippy Vibram rubber underneath.
Deep lugs that bite into mud, ideal for wet British winter trails.
Salomon's softest trail shoe, made for long days out when comfort matters most.
Gentle support with a wide front end, handy if your feet need space.
Flat, low and close to the ground with plenty of room for your toes.
Very soft and roomy up front, a rare mix of max cushion and toe space.
Light, simple and keenly priced, a solid choice for regular training runs.
Cushioned and steady, built for slow long runs rather than anything quick.
Made for proper mud, cross country and fell races where grip beats comfort.
The comfiest inov8, soft enough for all day hill days and long trail runs.
